source._php_version_note: composer.json config.platform.php = 8.3 and require php ^8.3; lib/versioncheck.php refuses PHP < 8.3 and >= 8.6. Since 2026-10-10 the image runs Ubuntu 24.04's own PHP 8.3 (it reports 8.3.6; Ubuntu backports security fixes into it) instead of the official php:8.4-apache-bookworm image, whose Debian 12 base our cerodeo-v1 scan grades F on vulnerabilities Debian does not fix. (Its recorded scan of v35.0.1-CE-debian-bookworm-r1: 30 unfixed critical, 172 unfixed high, 0 fixable.) 8.3 is exactly Nextcloud 35's floor, so a Nextcloud release that raises it cannot run on this image. PHP 8.4 on Ubuntu 24.04 would need a third-party archive (a PPA): a supply-chain decision, not taken here; preflight check_php BLOCKs a retarget whose source needs more than the image's PHP.
source._composer_note: NO `composer install` for the runtime: Nextcloud's runtime autoloader is 3rdparty/autoload.php and the 3rdparty git submodule IS the pre-vendored composer output (composer.json's lib/composer vendor-dir is only the bamarni dev bin plugin, not runtime). NO npm/webpack frontend build either: the built dist/ (sass css + esbuild js) is COMMITTED at the v34.0.1 tag (Makefile `clean-git: git checkout -- dist`). So the vendor stage = clone the tag + init the 3rdparty submodule, and the git tree + 3rdparty == the official signed nextcloud-34.0.1.tar.bz2 minus updater/. dep_bumps (composer CVE remediation) are applied IN the vendor stage by editing 3rdparty/composer.json (or the bundled app's composer.json) + running `composer update <pkg> --with-dependencies` inside that dir so installed.json + autoload regenerate (BOTH the on-disk files and the syft-read installed.json must change -- the L-026/php-composer-overlay rule).
source._build_packages_note: Vendor stage only: git + ca-certificates for the clone and the 3rdparty submodule (unzip for composer work inside 3rdparty). Nothing is compiled on the Ubuntu path, so there are no -dev packages; PHP, its extensions and Apache are runtime_packages, vendored as debs.
source._ext_note: Matches the upstream nextcloud/docker Dockerfile MINUS the external-DB exts (pdo_mysql/pdo_pgsql), ldap and imagick -- dropped for the lean SQLite-default CE image (Ubuntu's php8.3-common carries ftp, which upstream's image also has). source.php_extensions = composer.json's ext-* requirements + the extensions compiled until 2026-10-10 + pdo_sqlite/sqlite3 (the embedded database); the build asserts each is loaded in both the Apache and the CLI configuration. APCu is Ubuntu's php8.3-apcu 5.1.22 (universe; the pecl build before was 5.1.28); apc.enable_cli=1 is in nextcloud.ini because occ runs on the CLI.
source._prune_note: Strip dev/test/CI trees from the runtime image (the PHP CE-audit + size + Scout-noise reduction). `updater/` is removed exactly as the upstream image does (managed updates are out of scope for an immutable CE image). The committed dist/, 3rdparty/, apps/, core/, lib/, ocs/, ocs-provider/, resources/, themes/ + the root *.php / .htaccess / .user.ini / occ / robots.txt are KEPT (enumerated in app_copies).
